liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Dupree's Diamond Blues** (2 other sources): Jerry's voice was very rough during Dupree's, and he sang little or nothing after Uncle John's Band [4][5]
- **// Big Railroad Blues** (1 review): Jerry's vocal on Big Railroad Blues is singled out as laughably or painfully bad [37]
- **China Cat Sunflower** (1 review): The China Cat into Rider is called smoking, with audience reacting delightedly to Jerry's lead before I Know You Rider [32]
- **I Know You Rider** (1 review): First set was lackluster, but the China Cat into Rider was pretty good [36]
- **Drums** (1 review): A short, spooky-feeling jam comes right before the drums segment, which the reviewer especially remembers [29]

## The recordings

- **gd1985-04-06.aud.unknown.perkins.8900.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): audience recording; 22 songs; 134 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [1]. Said about its sound: Levels are low for roughly the first minute and a half of disc two track one; boosting was unsatisfactory [1]
- **gd1985-04-06.169897.matrix.miksis.miller.clugston.flac1648**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 19 songs; 144 min [4]. Said about its sound: Soundboard had ground hum and harmonics removed, plus de-clicking and pitch correction [4]
- **gd1985-04-06.170435.beyer.m160.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 19 songs; 141 min [5]
- **gd85-04-06.oade-schoeps.sacks.24027.sbeok.flacf**: source not stated; 20 songs; 144 min; rated 4.14/5 by 7 [13]. Said about its sound: Described as an excellent-sounding audience recording [38]
- **gd85-04-06.aud.barbella.10990.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 18 songs; 139 min; rated 3.33/5 by 6 [24]. Said about its sound: Audience recording captures the crowd's reaction, something the soundboard version lacks [32]

## Around the show

- Reviewer attended all three nights of the run and found this night well played [29]
- Jerry's voice was badly ruined on this night, with a rough moment in the Other One verse [31]
- Reviewer was at their sixth show and first of three consecutive nights of tickets [31]
- Show fell on Easter weekend in Philadelphia and opened a three-night run; Jerry's voice was rough but his playing was precise [32]
- Reviewer found the band flat and tired, playing poorly despite the strong China, Rider, Playin', Uncle John's sequence [35]
- Reviewer stood front row in front of Jerry on the general admission floor; Jerry's voice was shot and Bobby sprayed spit [36]
- With Jerry's voice shot, Bob sang the songs in the second half of the second set while Jerry played [38]
- The setlist is predictable and less impressive on paper than the next two nights, which used up common songs [29]
- Reviewer says the Sunday show was the best of the three-day set and had a slow Friend of the Devil [33]
- Reviewer says the Sunday show was the best of the three-day set and had a slow Friend of the Devil [34]
- Reviewer ranks this the worst of 200+ shows seen; the next two nights were much better, though none matched Nassau [35]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1985-04-06.aud.unknown.perkins.8900.sbeok.shnf**: source: unknown [1]
- **gd1985-04-06.169897.matrix.miksis.miller.clugston.flac1648**: source: SBD/AUD Matrix: Final Cut Pro (16b/48k) > Izotope RX Advanced > Peak Pro > xAct > FLAC/16 Created by Brian Miksis January 15, 2025 an archive.org user [4]. Also: Matrix of Charlie Miller's soundboard with Stephen Thomas's audience recording mastered by Scott Clugston, which covers soundboard tape flips [4]
- **gd1985-04-06.170435.beyer.m160.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Jim Vita; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Jim Vita's Master Audience Cassettes; Beyer M160 mics > Sony D5M (Maxell XLII-S) [5]. Also: A Sennheiser 441 source from Rob Hunt and Ted Mattes supplies a short patch in Space [5]
- **gd85-04-06.oade-schoeps.sacks.24027.sbeok.flacf**: taped by Oade Brothers; transferred by Doug Oade - Darren Sacks; source: Schoeps CMC441s (90deg, 17cm) > Oade M118 > Oade mod SONY PCM-F1 [13]
- **gd85-04-06.aud.barbella.10990.sbeok.shnf**: source: Master Audience Cassette>DAT>CDR [24]
